items.t: How Much Would You Need to Invest in Enbridge to Average $200 a Month?
sum: A company helping deliver energy to your home can also help pay the bills. The appealing part is getting cash without selling shares every month. The less attractive part is building the holding first. At the current payment and recent closing price, roughly $42,600 in one pipeline stock could produce a $200 monthly average, with the cash arriving quarterly.

A $200 monthly average means $2,400 a year. For a stock paying every three months, the practical target is about $600 each quarter. I’d collect the dividends in cash and make monthly transfers from that balance, giving my spending a smoother schedule than the company’s payment calendar.

Enbridge (TSX: ENB) makes that calculation possible with a quarterly dividend of $0.97 per share. Its annualized $3.88 payment yields about 5.6% at the recent closing price of $68.82. That’s substantial starting income, so the next step is making sure the business has room to pay it.

Enbridge operates oil and natural gas pipelines, gas utilities, and other energy infrastructure. Much of its earnings relies on regulated returns or contracted service, giving it a different relationship with oil prices from a producer selling the commodity. Customers pay for access to infrastructure they need to move and use energy.

Utilities and export facilities needing more gas capacity offer growth opportunities. Enbridge’s second-quarter update described new pipeline connections and expansions supported by customer demand. New assets can add earnings once operating, although construction spending comes before those earnings arrive.

For the dividend, management reaffirmed 2026 distributable cash flow of $5.70 to $6.10 per share. This is the company’s cash-flow measure after adjustments including maintenance spending and financing costs. The $3.88 annual dividend uses roughly 64% to 68% of that range, leaving some cash beyond the payment.
Reaching at least $2,400 annually requires 619 whole shares at the current payment. Using the recent close, and excluding trading fees, here’s the investment required.

Enbridge stock posts stronger Q3 and reaffirms 2026 outlook
sum: Enbridge reported stronger third-quarter results on Friday, November 6, 2026, and reaffirmed its full-year financial guidance. The release, carried by Finanznachrichten.de, covers the three months ended September 30 and cites Enbridge Inc. as the source.

Enbridge stock traded at 42.04 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 16:02 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026. That was 2.69 percent below the 43.20-euro quote in the latest relevant own report from November 4, a separate comparison from any Xetra session.

Adjusted EBITDA rose to CAD 4.434 billion from CAD 4.267 billion a year earlier. Adjusted earnings increased to CAD 1.074 billion, or CAD 0.49 per common share, while distributable cash flow reached CAD 2.689 billion compared with CAD 2.566 billion in the prior-year quarter.

GAAP earnings attributable to common shareholders climbed to CAD 1.288 billion from CAD 682 million. Enbridge said the comparison was helped by non-cash changes in the value of derivative instruments, so the adjusted measures provide the cleaner view of underlying quarterly performance.

The company placed the Aspen Point expansion of the B.C. Pipeline and the Tennessee Ridgeline project into service. It also announced the USD 2.6 billion acquisition of Tallgrass Energy's crude oil business, a USD 0.3 billion Pony Express expansion and a USD 0.5 billion agreement for Laramie Energy assets. The Salt Creek Midstream acquisition closed during the quarter.

Enbridge's secured growth backlog stands at approximately CAD 38 billion. The company reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of CAD 20.2 billion to CAD 20.8 billion and distributable cash flow per share guidance of CAD 5.70 to CAD 6.10. Its medium-term outlook still calls for average annual growth of approximately 5 percent across adjusted EBITDA, distributable cash flow per share and earnings per share.

The results strengthen the operating case, but the investment focus remains on execution, funding and integration. Enbridge completed a CAD 3.0 billion common equity offering to help fund recent transactions and said its secured growth program will be supported by annual growth capital capacity of CAD 10 billion to CAD 11 billion.

items.t: Inflation Is Heading to 3.5%: Yet These 2 Canadian Stocks Can Raise Prices and Keep Their Customers
sum: Canadians do not need a spreadsheet to know that prices are on the rise. They notice these trends at the pump and the grocery checkout.

Statistics Canada reported that consumer prices rose 3.1% year over year in September, up from 3.0% in August. On October 28, the Bank of Canada raised its policy rate by a quarter point to 2.50%, its first hike since July 2023.
The central bank also expects inflation to reach about 3.5% by the end of 2026. Moreover, the regulator does not see a return to its 2% target until mid-2028.
Given this macro backdrop, let’s see which companies are well positioned to pass higher costs to customers.
The Bank of Canada says inflation excluding gasoline was 2.2% in September, and the core measure remains close to 2%.
However, the central bank says high fuel prices are lifting production and transportation costs, which have been primarily absorbed by businesses.
Notably, companies that do not enjoy pricing power have seen profit margins shrink over the last six months.

Enbridge stock heads into November 6 results and webcast test
sum: Enbridge is heading into a major investor date next week: the Canadian energy infrastructure company will release its 2026 third-quarter results before markets open on Friday, November 6. In its October 5 announcement, Enbridge said the results would be followed by a business update and a question-and-answer session for analysts and investors.

The webcast and conference call are scheduled for 9 a.m. Eastern Time. The timing puts the earnings release ahead of the North American session and gives investors a defined event to assess operating performance, project execution and management commentary on demand for energy infrastructure.

Enbridge connects customers to energy through North American natural gas, oil and renewable power networks, as well as a European offshore wind portfolio. The company also highlights work on hydrogen, renewable natural gas and carbon capture and storage, broadening the strategic backdrop for the quarterly update.

For investors, the earnings release should clarify how the portfolio performed during the quarter and whether management changes its view on capital spending, project delivery or long-term energy demand. The conference call may add detail on the balance between established infrastructure assets and newer technologies.

Enbridge Announces CDN$2.6 Billion Bought-Deal Offering of Common Shares
sum: The Canadian base shelf prospectus is accessible, and the Canadian prospectus supplement or any amendment will be accessible, within two business days through SEDAR+.

CALGARY, AB, Sept. 9, 2026 /CNW/ -- Enbridge Inc. (TSX: ENB) (NYSE: ENB) ("Enbridge" or the "Company") today announced that it has entered into an agreement with a syndicate of underwriters (the "Underwriters") led by RBC Capital Markets and CIBC Capital Markets, and including Scotiabank, BMO Capital Markets, TD Securities Inc., and National Bank of Canada Capital Markets as joint bookrunners, under which the Underwriters have agreed to purchase, on a bought deal basis, 38,900,000 common shares of the Company ("Common Shares") for aggregate gross proceeds of CDN$2.6 billion at an offering price of CDN$66.85 per Common Share (the "Offering").

Enbridge intends to use the net proceeds from the Offering to partially fund announced acquisitions and to create financial flexibility to fund potential future growth opportunities. A portion of the net proceeds of the Offering may be temporarily used to reduce indebtedness or invested in short-term liquid investments.

The Common Shares will be offered to the public in all of the provinces of Canada through the Underwriters and their affiliates by way of a Canadian prospectus supplement (the "Canadian Prospectus Supplement") to Enbridge's short form base shelf prospectus dated September 9, 2026 (the "Canadian Prospectus"). The Common Shares will be offered to the public in the United States pursuant to Enbridge's registration statement, including a prospectus (the "U.S. Prospectus"), filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC"), and a prospectus supplement (the "U.S. Prospectus Supplement") to the U.S. Prospectus. Before investing, prospective purchasers in Canada should read the Canadian Prospectus Supplement, the Canadian Prospectus and the documents incorporated by reference therein, and prospective purchasers in the United States should read the U.S. Prospectus, the U.S. Prospectus Supplement and the documents incorporated by reference therein for more complete information about Enbridge and the Offering in Canada and the United States, respectively.
